title: Finite-order convolution and tangent derivations for a commutative bialgebra
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a commutative unital $k$-algebra with unital algebra maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ and $\varepsilon:C\to k$ satisfying coassociativity and the two counit identities $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=1_C$, using the canonical tensor identifications [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the commutative $k$-algebra structure on $C\otimes_kC$ with $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$ and unit $1\otimes1$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Put $I=\ker\varepsilon$ and
$$F_n=\{a\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(C,k):a(I^{n+1})=0\},\quad F_{-1}=0,\quad F=\bigcup_{n\geq0}F_n.$$
For $a,b:C\to k$ linear set $(a*b)(c)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta c)$. This makes $F$ a unital associative $k$-algebra with unit $\varepsilon$, and $F_r*F_s\subseteq F_{r+s}$ for $r,s\geq0$.
Let $L$ be the vector space of linear maps $v:C\to k$ satisfying $v(ab)=\varepsilon(a)v(b)+v(a)\varepsilon(b)$. Restriction identifies $L$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_k(I/I^2,k)$; in particular $L\subseteq F_1$ and $v(1)=0$. The map
$$v\longmapsto D_v=(1\otimes v)\Delta$$
is a linear bijection from $L$ to the $k$-linear derivations $D:C\to C$ (that is, $D(ab)=aD(b)+D(a)b$) satisfying $\Delta D=(1\otimes D)\Delta$, with inverse $D\mapsto\varepsilon D$. Commutators of these derivations remain of this kind, and the bracket defined by $D_{[v,w]}=D_vD_w-D_wD_v$ makes $L$ a Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra] and satisfies $[v,w]=v*w-w*v$.

source.place: Sections 10e and 10l, Proposition 10.29 and printed pp.195--196, 208: left-invariant derivations and the filtered convolution algebra. Bialgebra generality isolates precisely the axioms used; inverse map epsilon D and bracket follow the displayed coassociativity computation.

proof.text: Write $\eta:k\to C$ for the scalar map and $p(c)=c-\varepsilon(c)1$. Since $\varepsilon\eta=1_k$, every $c$ has the unique decomposition $\varepsilon(c)1+p(c)$ with $p(c)\in I$. Thus $C=k1\oplus I$. The bilinearity relations for tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] expand every tensor into its four $k1,I$ slots; the projections are the tensor products of $\eta\varepsilon$ and $p$.

source.place: §10(l), printed p.208, augmentation splitting; explicit scalar and augmentation projections

proof.text: For $x\in I$, the scalar–scalar slot of $\Delta x$ is zero, since $(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta x=\varepsilon(x)=0$. Each of the remaining three slots has at least one factor in $I$. Consequently $\Delta(I)\subseteq I\otimes C+C\otimes I$, with the right side denoting the sum of the images in $C\otimes C$. These inclusions and expansions use only the tensor bilinearity of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: §10(l), printed p.208, order filtration; explicit augmentation-slot expansion

proof.text: Let $a\in F_r$, $b\in F_s$ and $N=r+s+1$. For $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in I$, multiplicativity of $\Delta$ for the product $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$ of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $\Delta(x_1\cdots x_N)=\prod_j\Delta(x_j)$. Expand using Step 2. Each term has at least $N$ occurrences of factors from $I$ distributed over its two slots, so either the first slot belongs to $I^{r+1}$ or the second belongs to $I^{s+1}$. Thus $(a\otimes b)$ kills every term. Products of $N$ elements of $I$ span $I^N$ (absorb an arbitrary coefficient in one factor), so $a*b\in F_{r+s}$.

source.place: §10(l), printed p.208, filtered convolution; expanded product and pigeonhole argument

proof.text: The coalgebra axioms in the hypotheses allow [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra] with $R=B=k$: the full linear dual has the specified associative unital convolution algebra structure, unit $\varepsilon$, and scalar map $t\mapsto t\varepsilon$. Each $F_n$ is a vector subspace and $F_n\subseteq F_{n+1}$ since $I^{n+2}\subseteq I^{n+1}$. Their union is a vector subspace; Step 3 makes it closed under multiplication, and $\varepsilon\in F_0$. Restrict the full-dual operations and identities to this union to obtain the asserted filtered algebra.

source.place: §10(l), printed p.208; full-dual algebra supplied by the cited convolution lemma

proof.text: For $v\in L$, substituting $a=b=1$ gives $v(1)=2v(1)$, hence $v(1)=0$ in every characteristic. For $x,y\in I$, the defining Leibniz identity gives $v(xy)=0$, so $v$ kills $I^2$. Its restriction therefore factors through $I/I^2$, and $v\in F_1$. Since $v$ kills scalars, the decomposition in Step 1 shows that this restriction determines $v$.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.28 and §10(l), printed pp.195,208; direct Leibniz calculation

proof.text: Conversely, for $\lambda:I/I^2\to k$ linear put $v_\lambda(c)=\lambda(p(c)\bmod I^2)$. The equality $p(ab)=\varepsilon(a)p(b)+p(a)\varepsilon(b)+p(a)p(b)$ implies $v_\lambda(ab)=\varepsilon(a)v_\lambda(b)+v_\lambda(a)\varepsilon(b)$. These two constructions are linear and inverse, since $p(x)=x$ for $x\in I$ and every $v\in L$ kills scalars. This proves exactly the asserted linear identification of $L$ with the cotangent dual.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.28 and §10(l), printed pp.195,208; explicit inverse on the augmentation summand

proof.text: Use finite-sum notation $\Delta a=\sum a_1\otimes a_2$ (each tensor is a finite sum of simple tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]). For $v\in L$, multiplicativity of $\Delta$ for the tensor-algebra product of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and the Leibniz identity of $v$ give $D_v(ab)=\sum a_1b_1(\varepsilon(a_2)v(b_2)+v(a_2)\varepsilon(b_2))=aD_v(b)+D_v(a)b$ by the two counit contractions. Thus the displayed $k$-linear map $D_v$ is a derivation.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.29, printed pp.195–196; explicit bialgebra calculation

proof.text: Applying $1\otimes1\otimes v$ to $(\Delta\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\Delta)\Delta$ gives $\Delta D_v=(1\otimes D_v)\Delta$. Moreover $\varepsilon D_v(c)=\sum\varepsilon(c_1)v(c_2)=v(c)$ by the other counit contraction. These formulas show invariance and one of the inverse identities; linearity in $v$ follows from the formula for $D_v$.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.29, printed pp.195–196; explicit bialgebra calculation

proof.text: If $D:C\to C$ is a $k$-linear derivation with $\Delta D=(1\otimes D)\Delta$, the map $v=\varepsilon D$ belongs to $L$, because $\varepsilon$ is multiplicative and $\varepsilon(D(ab))=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(Db)+\varepsilon(Da)\varepsilon(b)$. Applying $1\otimes\varepsilon$ to the invariance equation gives $D=(1\otimes\varepsilon D)\Delta=D_v$. Together with Step 8 this proves the stated linear bijection and its inverse.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.29, printed pp.195–196; explicit bialgebra calculation

proof.text: For invariant derivations $D,E$ put $H=DE-ED$. Expanding both iterated Leibniz formulas cancels the two cross terms, giving $H(ab)=aH(b)+H(a)b$. Also $\Delta DE=(1\otimes D)\Delta E=(1\otimes DE)\Delta$, and likewise for $ED$; subtraction gives $\Delta H=(1\otimes H)\Delta$. Hence the subspace of invariant derivations is closed under commutators.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.29, printed pp.195–196; explicit bialgebra calculation

proof.text: The statement of [def-wf-lie-algebra] gives the commutator Lie algebra of $\operatorname{End}_k(C)$ and every commutator-closed subspace. Apply it to the subspace in Step 10, and transport its bracket through the linear bijection of Steps 8–9. Bilinearity, alternation and Jacobi are preserved by this bijection, and by construction $D_{[v,w]}=D_vD_w-D_wD_v$.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.29, printed pp.195–196; explicit bialgebra calculation

proof.text: Finally, for $\Delta c=\sum c_1\otimes c_2$, linearity and $\varepsilon D_v=v$ give $\varepsilon(D_vD_w(c))=\sum\varepsilon(D_v(c_1))w(c_2)=\sum v(c_1)w(c_2)=(v*w)(c)$. Interchanging $v,w$ and subtracting, then using the inverse $D\mapsto\varepsilon D$, proves $[v,w]=v*w-w*v$ with the asserted order of the factors.

source.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.29, printed pp.195–196; explicit bialgebra calculation

proof_origin.place: §10(e), Proposition 10.28–10.29, printed pp.195–196, and §10(l), printed p.208; omitted tensor and filtration calculations expanded explicitly using precisely the bialgebra axioms.

lean.statement: theorem finiteOrderConvolutionAndTangentDerivations (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [Bialgebra k C] : (∃ S : Subalgebra k (WithConv (C →ₗ[k] k)), (∀ a : WithConv (C →ₗ[k] k), a ∈ S ↔ a.ofConv ∈ distributions k C) ∧ (∀ r s : ℕ, ∀ a b : C →ₗ[k] k, a ∈ finiteOrder k C r → b ∈ finiteOrder k C s → convolution k C a b ∈ finiteOrder k C (r + s)) ∧ ((1 : WithConv (C →ₗ[k] k)).ofConv = Coalgebra.counit (R := k) (A := C))) ∧ (∃ e : tangentFunctionals k C ≃ₗ[k] Module.Dual k (augmentationIdeal k C).Cotangent, (∀ v : tangentFunctionals k C, ∀ x : augmentationIdeal k C, e v ((augmentationIdeal k C).toCotangent x) = v.1 x.1)) ∧ (∃ M : Submodule k (Derivation k C C), (∀ D : Derivation k C C, D ∈ M ↔ invariantDerivation k C D) ∧ (∃ eD : tangentFunctionals k C ≃ₗ[k] M, (∀ v : tangentFunctionals k C, (eD v).1.toLinearMap = tangentContraction k C v.1) ∧ (∀ D : M, (eD.symm D).1 = Coalgebra.counit.comp D.1.toLinearMap))) ∧ (∀ v : tangentFunctionals k C, v.1 ∈ finiteOrder k C 1 ∧ v.1 1 = 0) ∧ (∀ D E : Derivation k C C, invariantDerivation k C D → invariantDerivation k C E → invariantDerivation k C ⁅D, E⁆) ∧ (∃ LR : LieRing (tangentFunctionals k C), LR.toAddCommGroup = (inferInstance : AddCommGroup (tangentFunctionals k C)) ∧ ∃ LA : @LieAlgebra k (tangentFunctionals k C) _ LR, HEq LA.toModule (inferInstance : Module k (tangentFunctionals k C)) ∧ ∀ v w : tangentFunctionals k C, (@Bracket.bracket _ _ LR.toBracket v w).1 = convolution k C v.1 w.1 - convolution k C w.1 v.1 ∧ tangentContraction k C (@Bracket.bracket _ _ LR.toBracket v w).1 = (tangentContraction k C v.1).comp (tangentContraction k C w.1) - (tangentContraction k C w.1).comp (tangentContraction k C v.1))
